pass_condition: Blocks the stop when U+2014 or U+2013 appears in the last assistant text after fenced blocks and inline code spans are blanked. This is a text check, but the text IS the deliverable the rule governs: there is no gap between 'writing the right string' and 'doing the work', so knowing the pattern is compliance, not evasion. Only carve-out: a dash inside backticks, which is the documented data case.
structural_check: Measured property of the artifact itself (the reply), read from the transcript rather than self-reported.

pass_condition: A newly-ticked `- [x]` line in _plans/*.md passes if that line (or one of the next 2 continuation lines) matches EVIDENCE = a 7-40 char hex run, OR a `<name>.<ext>:<digits>` token, OR the literal `verified:`/`proof:`/`measured:`/`confirmed:`; nothing is opened, resolved, or compared against the repo.

A fabricated file:line (`Foo.tsx:999`) and a fake sha both pass, and the docstring's own founding case (`ServicesStaffStep.tsx` never imported the module) would pass today by appending `verified:` to the same false tick.

pass_condition: Fires on a defect assertion near a repo noun in the final message, then exits 0 if EVIDENCE matches ANYWHERE in that same message: the bare words verified/measured/proved, `I checked|ran|read|queried`, any `\d+/\d+`, or any comma-grouped number like 2,981.
structural_check: none - the gate never looks at the transcript, so no tool call, query, or file read is required. `\b\d+\s*/\s*\d+\b` means an incidental "5/5" or "19/19" anywhere in the reply exempts every defect claim in it, and the block text hands over the exact wording: 'or an explicit "I verified / I measured / I checked / I ran"'.

pass_condition: A mockup HTML write passes if it contains >=1 `Diagnosis:` line carrying the substrings measured + violates + target, and the normalized measured-value differs from the normalized target-value.
beating_phrase: <!-- Diagnosis: team card | measured rounded-3xl+shadow-float | violates LOCKFILE:427 | target rounded-24+border+shadow-whisper -->
structural_check: none - no page is rendered, no value is read back, and the cited LOCKFILE line is never opened or checked to exist. The only real test is cur != tgt, i.e. the invented numbers must merely disagree with each other. The gate exists because the assistant INVENTS instead of measuring, and an invented pair of numbers satisfies it (the quoted phrase is lifted verbatim from the gate's own self-test).

pass_condition: When the owner's message carries correction language plus (noun, colour) pairs, the stop passes if the final reply contains the noun-synonym AND the colour-synonym somewhere in it - anywhere, unordered, not adjacent, no claim of application required.
beating_phrase: roads are now gray, tiles white, blue dots
structural_check: none - no file, diff, or rendered pixel is inspected; the reply merely has to echo the owner's own vocabulary back. Note the block message prints the winning sentence verbatim ('e.g. roads are now gray, tiles white, blue dots'), so the gate teaches its own bypass. "the tiles are unchanged and the dots are still blue" also passes.

pass_condition: From the 3rd same-subject fix claim in a session (counted structurally over the transcript's assistant messages), the stop passes if the closing reply matches ROOT_CAUSE - which includes the bare tokens `simpler`, `removed`, `deleted`, `the cause`, and `instead of`.
structural_check: real: it counts prior assistant closing messages that claimed a fix about the same subject noun, from the transcript on disk - that count cannot be faked. But the escape is a two-word English phrase that appears in ordinary technical prose, so the gate is effectively inert; any attempt-3 reply containing "instead of" or "removed" is waved through with no step-back at all.

pass_condition: A .tsx/.jsx hand-building a salon card (a / whose next 24 lines hold /salon/ plus a raw ) is blocked - unless the payload text contains the substring "SalonCard" anywhere, or the marker `registered-component-ok`.
structural_check: real: it parses the written markup for a link+image window, which is an actual code-structure fact and cannot be talked away. The hole is line 72, `if "SalonCard" in text: return []` - intended as "the file composes the real component", it accepts the bare token in a comment. The gate's own deny text pushes the assistant toward naming SalonCard, so the natural repair-shaped comment permanently silences it while the hand-built card ships.

pass_condition: A paint/occlusion claim about a fixed/sticky/overlay element blocks only if the turn shows a geometry read AND no PAINT_PROOF match; PAINT_PROOF includes the bare word `screenshot` and any `.png`, matched over the whole turn blob including the assistant's own prose.
structural_check: real: the turn blob is the transcript since the last user message, so a genuine elementFromPoint eval or screenshot tool call registers as proof. Two holes: (1) the escape is the bare word, so even "no screenshot needed here" satisfies the paint proof; (2) the gate returns None when no geometry read is present, so a claim made with NO measurement at all - the worse case - is never examined.

pass_condition: A Write to _plans/ACTIVE.md passes iff the new content contains the literal substring WORKSTREAMS-INDEX; nothing compares the new content against the rows currently in the file.
structural_check: none - a single-plan overwrite that drops every existing workstream row passes as long as it carries the marker, which is exactly the clobber the guard was born for ('plans get lost'). The deny message states the bypass outright: 'If you truly mean to rewrite the index, keep the marker line.' Edit/MultiEdit are out of scope by design.

pass_condition: A scripts/*.mjs that both navigates a browser and prints a verdict is blocked unless GUARDED matches anywhere in the payload: `_measure-guard`, `guardedGoto`, a `.status() >= 4xx` comparison, `response.ok`, or any `.ok()`.
beating_phrase: // guardedGoto not needed here, the page is static
structural_check: real for the trigger and partly for the escape: `.status() >= 400` is an actual status check in real code. But the token match is not scoped to executable code, so a comment naming guardedGoto, or an unrelated `.ok()` call anywhere in the file, satisfies it - the script can still measure a 500 error page and print VERDICT PASS.

pass_condition: An Agent/Workflow call whose model contains 'opus' is denied unless the prompt+description text matches JUDGMENT (judge, score, critique, verdict, taste, design review, decide between, or the literal tag [judgment]).
structural_check: real: the model field of the actual tool call is read (and 'fable'/'mythos' is denied unconditionally, with no text escape). The routing half is text-only - the deny message says 'or tag the prompt [judgment] if it genuinely is one', so a mechanical build dispatch reaches opus by adding six characters.

pass_condition: Advisory only (always emits allow). It stays silent when the added text contains any WARNING_MARKER - which includes `never`, `do not`, `don't`, `wrong`, `dangerous`, `no longer`, `deprecated` - anywhere in the same block as the antipattern.
structural_check: real: it detects concrete constructs (getSession( plus identity markers, DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, NEXT_PUBLIC_*service_role, admin client in a 'use client' file). The warning-marker suppressor is block-wide, so one ordinary comment such as "this should never fail" beside a getSession() identity read silences it. Consequence is capped: it never blocks, and the project's no-getsession-authz-gate blocks the code case.

pass_condition: A mockup HTML write is blocked iff its text contains one of ~15 English phrases (flatten, borderless, chrome off, remove the card, de-card, no shadow, `box-shadow: none`, un-card); everything else passes.
beating_phrase: var CHANGE_LABEL='After: cleaner section rhythm'; /* border:0; box-shadow:0 0 0 transparent */
structural_check: none - the regex reads the mockup's self-description (CHANGE_LABEL, comments), not its rendered treatment. The single style token it does catch, `box-shadow: none`, is trivially expressed as `box-shadow:0 0 0 transparent` or camelCase `boxShadow:'none'` (the hyphen is required to match), so the ditched flat direction ships as long as it is not named.

pass_condition: Blocks only when the final reply matches REMOVAL_CLAIM (I removed/deleted/dropped/pulled, is now gone/disabled, shipping without, left it out) AND the owner's last message matches no removal order; a reply that does not use those verbs is never examined.
beating_phrase: The air isn't in the current version.
structural_check: none for the assistant's half - no diff, git status, or file read confirms whether anything was actually deleted. There is one unfakeable input (the owner's own last message is parsed from the transcript for a removal order), but it is only consulted after the reply's phrasing has already triggered; a paraphrased removal never reaches it.

pass_condition: Blocks the stop when any mockup/component file modified in the last 15 min contains #276EF1 or text-s-accent within ~160 chars of a parenthesized number with no intervening `<`; otherwise exits 0.
structural_check: It reads the bytes of files on disk (mtime-filtered) and matches the actual paint tokens next to the actual count markup - the styling IS the thing being regulated, so there is no phrase that makes a bare-accent count pass. Weaknesses are coverage, not satisfiability: an equivalent hex written differently, or a count painted via a variable/class indirection, is not seen.

pass_condition: Denies a Solen /_mockups/ html write whose post-edit content has a CSS rule combining width 380-440px with border-radius >= 30px, or status-bar chrome markers (island/batt/status-bar/signalbar classes, or a bare >HH:MM< node).
structural_check: It matches measured CSS declarations and real DOM markers in the artifact, and for Edit/MultiEdit it reconstructs the post-edit file from disk rather than trusting the fragment. Evasion needs genuinely different code (width:25rem, border-radius:2rem), not a claim. Worth fixing: the docstring advertises an escape - "put `real-phone-ok` in the content" - that is not implemented anywhere in the code; only the skip flag exists.

pass_condition: Denies a write under /dev/search-morph/ whose added content has an onWheel/onTouchMove/onScroll handler whose body within 800 chars calls setInputFocused(true); anything else passes.
structural_check: It matches the actual banned wiring construct (JSX handler -> state setter), including new_string inside MultiEdit edits[], so passing requires writing different code, not different prose. Coverage gap only: an addEventListener('wheel', ...) binding, a differently-named setter, or a handler extracted to a helper is not matched.

pass_condition: Denies a Bash call whose command (heredoc bodies stripped) matches an image-generation signature: dall-e, images/generations, /v1/images, stable-diffusion, midjourney, flux-schnell|dev|pro, gemini-*-image, responseModalities image, or imagen with version/API context.
structural_check: It inspects the literal command about to execute, so the match is close to definitional - there is no sentence that makes a dall-e call pass. Two real gaps, both channel-shaped rather than phrase-shaped: it only fires on tool_name == Bash, so the MCP image-generation tools (generate_image / generate_image_batch) are entirely outside its scope, and a URL assembled from variables evades the literal patterns.

pass_condition: Auto-allows an edit when os.path.realpath of the target sits under a trusted root inside a .claude/{hooks,skills,agents,commands,workflows,projects} segment, ~/.vscode/extensions, or is a top-level ~/.claude/*.md|*.txt; stays silent (modal stands) otherwise.
structural_check: Every decision is a resolved-path fact: realpath collapses .. and symlinks, and settings.json / settings.local.json / .mcp.json / ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md / .git are refused by basename before any allow branch runs, so self-granting always costs a human click. Nothing here can be argued into allowing a path.

pass_condition: Once per 24h it runs `node scripts/check-invariants.mjs` and prints a heads-up only when the process exit code is non-zero; never blocks anything.
structural_check: Satisfaction is a real subprocess exit code - one of the few checks in this batch whose verdict is produced by executing something rather than by reading text. It also correctly writes the throttle stamp only after the run, so a timeout retries next session instead of going silent for a day.

pass_condition: Never blocks: on a Write of a new top-level ~/.claude/hooks/*.py it globs the existing hooks and emits an allow-with-nudge when basename stems or >=2 distinctive tokens overlap; silent otherwise.
structural_check: The overlap test is computed from the actual filenames present on disk plus the new file's own first 40 lines, so the nudge cannot be argued away - though it is advisory by design, so nothing is enforced either way. Naming a duplicate gate with disjoint tokens avoids the nudge, but that is a detection gap in an advisory, not a pass condition being faked.

pass_condition: No verdict at all - it always exits 0 after writing epoch time to ~/.claude/state/planfirst-<session_id>.stamp plus the legacy global stamp.
structural_check: It produces a real timestamp file (session-keyed, so concurrent worktree sessions no longer stomp each other) that plan-first-gate.py consumes as its structural baseline. It accepts nothing and blocks nothing, so there is nothing here to satisfy with a phrase.

pass_condition: Never blocks - on a UserPromptSubmit matching VARIATION + MOCKUP_CTX + UI_ANCHOR it injects a mandate to produce >=3 distinct directions, then exits 0.
structural_check: none in the enforcement sense: it is an injector whose trigger reads the OWNER's prompt (not assistant output), so the assistant cannot beat it by writing anything. Worth recording that the mandate it injects - 3 distinct variations, side by side, clickable - is verified by no check anywhere; producing one synthesized mockup instead has no consequence.

pass_condition: Never blocks - on owner rejection/redesign language (strong triggers alone, weak triggers only with a design-context word) it injects the structure-liberty directive plus six standing mockup rules, then exits 0.
structural_check: none in the enforcement sense: trigger is a regex over the OWNER's prompt, so nothing the assistant writes affects it, and it enforces nothing afterward. One robustness defect: `from notification_guard import is_notification_prompt` sits at module top OUTSIDE any try (line 15), so a missing/broken _lib crashes the hook before its own try block - the sibling mockup-variations.py documents this exact bug as fixed on 2026-07-10 and wraps its import; this file never got the fix.

pass_condition: Blocks the final message only when it contains >=2 APOLOGY matches, or 1 plus a STRONG_GROVEL match; a reply with at most one apology phrase and no groveling passes.
beating_phrase: That was my mistake, here is the fix.
structural_check: none - it is a pure ceiling on words in the reply. The quoted phrase matches zero APOLOGY alternatives ("my mistake" is not in the pattern), so it passes, as does a reply with no ownership and no fix at all: rule 17's substantive half (name what went wrong, then give the fix) is unverified. Low severity because the check is close to coextensive with the behaviour it bans - not apologizing twice IS the compliance.
